observations: Three photos show a used (tokunbo) 4-cylinder car engine photographed in what looks like an engine-parts yard/warehouse, with other engines stacked behind it.
Photo 0 shows the top of the engine block with exposed intake ports, rust and corrosion staining around the manifold area, and a watermark 'SOMTO GREAT'.
Photo 1 shows the timing cover, alternator, belt and pulleys, with visible surface rust on bolts and metal surfaces.
Photo 2 shows the engine from the exhaust manifold/valve cover side, wiring harness still attached, a person standing in the background, and heavy belt covering part of the frame.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, or any stamped identification number is visible or legible in any of the three photos.
No photo shows the engine running, being started, or any compression/leak test.

identity.kind: used (tokunbo) 4-cylinder car engine, claimed for Hyundai Elantra 2012/13

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show visible rust/corrosion on the manifold area and bolts, and surface grime consistent with a used, not pristine, engine.
No import documentation, customs paperwork, or shipping tag is visible in any photo; origin cannot be confirmed from images alone.
No engine code plate, VIN sticker, or any legible identifying mark tying this block to a Hyundai Elantra 2012/13 is visible in photos 0, 1, or 2.
No price-data comparison possible from photos; price claims are outside scope of visual verification.

risks.risk: Engine may not actually match a Hyundai Elantra 2012/13 (wrong engine code/displacement), which would drastically affect value and fitment.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code/ID plate or casting number stamped on the block.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unverified/unknown-fitment used engine, not confirmed Elantra-specific

risks.risk: Mechanical condition unknown — engine could be seized, have internal damage, or fail compression despite external cleanliness claims.
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine being started and running, or a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Visible rust and corrosion around intake/manifold area may indicate water damage or prolonged outdoor storage affecting internals.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder head surface and oil/coolant passages, plus oil dipstick condition.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having potential internal corrosion damage

risks.risk: Engine may be missing accessories (turbo, sensors, ECU, wiring harness completeness) typically bundled with 'complete engine' sales.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set showing all sides including intake, exhaust, and accessory brackets.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine code/ID plate or stamped casting number on the block
Video of the engine running (cold start) with audible sound
Close-up of the cylinder head/manifold corrosion area and oil dipstick
Full set of photos showing all sides of the engine including any missing accessories
response.reason: No VIN, engine code, or identification plate is legible in any photo, so the Hyundai Elantra fitment claim that would set the correct price bracket cannot even be assessed at a worst-case level; a close-up of the engine code is required before pricing.
